sections.html: The Blue-eyed Panaque was in the 1980s one of the most common loricariids in the trade. The correct scientific name is Panaque suttonorum. For unknown reasons the fish is hardly available nowadays, and there are many rumours: some say an ecological catastrophe occurred, others that the river was poisoned and all fish killed, and another that the Colombian drug mafia controls the area where the fish occurs. Whatever the truth, the species cannot be extinct in the wild, as a few specimens are still obtained now and then. A beautiful individual with bright blue eyes, about 20-25 cm long, has been seen.
